style: Organized, combative side under Graham Arnold built on defensive solidity and a clear focal point in target striker Aymen Hussein. Looks to play direct and use Ali Jasim's creativity in transition; physically committed but limited depth of attacking quality.
recent_form: Reached their first World Cup since 1986 after winning the intercontinental playoff final against Bolivia, with Aymen Hussein scoring the decisive goal. Lost a 2-0 friendly to Venezuela in Chicago on June 10, dropping to 57th.

key_players.name: Aymen Hussein
key_players.note: Top scorer in Asian qualifying with eight goals and scorer of the playoff winner v Bolivia; the team's main attacking outlet.

key_players.name: Ali Al-Hamadi
key_players.note: First Iraqi to play in the Premier League (Ipswich Town); pace and finishing to complement Hussein.

key_players.name: Ali Jasim
key_players.note: Creative spark on the flank who headlines the squad's attacking talent.

key_players.name: Amir Al-Ammari
key_players.note: Midfield string-puller who dictates tempo and links defence to attack.

key_players.name: Jalal Hassan
key_players.note: Captain and leader of the team from between the posts.

historical_news: Returned to the World Cup for the first time since 1986, a 40-year absence.
Sealed qualification by winning the intercontinental playoff final against Bolivia.
Aymen Hussein scored both the playoff winner and topped Asian qualifying with eight goals.
Coached by Australian Graham Arnold into the finals.
Drawn into Group I, where they are the lowest-ranked side, facing Norway, France and others.

media_sentiment.label: positive
media_sentiment.summary: Jubilant Iraqi sentiment over ending a four-decade World Cup wait, with national pride centered on Aymen Hussein; tempered realism after the pre-tournament loss to Venezuela and being the lowest seed in their group.
